newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Mutual said to seek group talks on Big Bang.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Mutual said to seek group talks on Big Bang.

text.p: The president of Mitsui Mutual Life Insurance Co said on Friday that he wanted to consult financial institutions within the Mitsui group about how to deal with Japan's "Big Bang" reforms, Jiji news agency said.

Koshiro Tsuchida, president of Japan's sixth biggest life insurer, was quoted as saying that he wanted to discuss the issue with four financial institutions in the Mitsui group, including Sakura Bank Ltd and Mitsui Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd.

It is possible that the group companies might set up a holding company centred on Sakura Bank, and the group financial institutions would discuss such an issue in the context of the Big Bang, Jiji quoted Tsuchida as saying.

Tsuchida spoke to reporters at a news conference announcing a management change at Mitsui Mutual, in which Tsuchida will become chairman and a senior managing director, Akira Miake, will become president from April 1, it said.
A spokeswoman at Mitsui Mutual confirmed the personnel change but could not confirm Tsuchida's comments.
Comments from Sakura Bank were not immediately available.

Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its political allies agreed on Tuesday to lift a 50-year-old ban on holding companies, enabling the government to submit a bill to parliament in March. The bill is expected to take effect early next year.
The Finance Ministry has also begun to work out guidelines and necessary revisions to financial laws to enable financial institutions to set up financial holding companies.
